set.scope: familiar contexts for constant ratio

set.reason: The criteria identify an invariant ratio and use its value to find the other quantity. This requires the quotient meaning of a ratio, without the additional cross-product property of proportions. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
set.scope: Interpreting the constant ratio and using its value in direct proportion

set.reason: The target explicitly forms a proportion and finds its unknown, containing proportion solving as a required final component.
set.scope: setting up and solving the proportion

set.reason: The explicit criterion distinguishes direct from inverse proportion and uses the selected relation. Direct-proportion meaning is necessary for the direct branch and for the stated comparison.
set.scope: judging direct proportion and setting up its proportion

set.reason: The same explicit comparison requires inverse-proportion meaning; calling it merely optional would omit part of the actual criterion.
set.scope: distinguishing direct from inverse proportion

set.reason: The example illustrates an estimate, while the general purpose is not confined to summation. Approximate sums illustrate estimation but do not define all estimation tasks. A length estimate or a rough product estimate can teach the purpose without this addition procedure.
set.scope: rounding-based approximate sums as one example
